paragraphs.title: Tradition and Its Lesson for Future Generations

easy.explanation: He says, “Give ear, O my people, to my law.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the people to hear?

easy.explanation: The fathers had told them the works of God.
easy.q: Who told the people what they had heard and known?

answers: The praises and wonderful works of the LORD
easy.explanation: They were to show the next generation the LORD’s praises, strength, and wonderful works.
easy.q: What were the fathers to show to the generation to come?

answers: So they would set their hope in God and keep His commandments
So they would forget the past
medium.explanation: The purpose was that they might hope in God, remember His works, and keep His commandments.
medium.q: Why were God’s works to be made known to future generations?

answers: The coming generation would wander, but their fathers would settle
The coming generation should trust and obey, unlike the stubborn fathers
The coming generation would rule, but their fathers would serve
medium.explanation: The people were warned not to be like their stubborn and rebellious fathers.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the coming generation and their fathers?

answers: To trust God for help and faithfulness
medium.explanation: Setting hope in God means trusting Him rather than forgetting His works.
medium.q: In verse 7, what does “set their hope in God” mean?

answers: Remembering God’s works should lead to hope and obedience
Remembering the past leads people away from God
challenge.explanation: The account was preserved so later generations would trust God and keep His commandments.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between remembering the past and future conduct?

answers: Tradition was meant for one generation only
Responsibility for remembering God passes from generation to generation
Children had no part in the tradition
challenge.explanation: Each generation was to teach the next what God had done.
challenge.q: What does the repeated passing of the testimony from fathers to children emphasize?

answers: Their heart was not right and their spirit was not steadfast with God
challenge.explanation: Their hearts were not set aright, and their spirit was not steadfast with God.
challenge.q: What is the main criticism of the “stubborn and rebellious generation”?

paragraphs.title: The Rebellion of Ephraim and Forgetting the Wonders

easy.explanation: They “turned back in the day of battle.”
easy.q: What did the children of Ephraim do in battle?

easy.explanation: The verse says they kept not the covenant of God.
easy.q: What did they fail to keep?

easy.explanation: They forgot the works and wonders that God had shown them.
easy.q: What did they forget?

medium.explanation: The passage places their failure to keep the covenant alongside their forgetting God’s works.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between forgetting God’s works and breaking His covenant?

medium.explanation: God had done marvelous things before their fathers in Egypt.
medium.q: What wonders had their fathers seen?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes armed warriors carrying bows.
medium.q: What does “armed, and carrying bows” describe?

answers: They were equipped for battle but turned back
They had never heard of Egypt
challenge.explanation: Although armed and carrying bows, they turned back in the day of battle.
challenge.q: What paradox appears in the description of Ephraim?

answers: Their forgetfulness was serious despite the historical witness of God’s miracles
challenge.explanation: They forgot wonders that God had performed before their fathers in Egypt.
challenge.q: Why is Egypt mentioned in connection with Ephraim’s forgetfulness?

answers: Outward ability cannot replace faithfulness to God
challenge.explanation: Their failure was connected to unfaithfulness, not a lack of weapons.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from joining military ability with unfaithfulness?

paragraphs.title: Wonders in the Wilderness and Rebellion

easy.explanation: He divided the sea and caused the people to pass through.
easy.q: What did God do to the sea?

answers: By a cloud and a light of fire
easy.explanation: He led them with a cloud by day and fire by night.
easy.q: How did God lead them by day and by night?

easy.explanation: They asked for meat for their lust.
easy.q: What did the people ask for in the wilderness?

answers: God brought streams from the rock
medium.explanation: God brought streams out of the rock and caused waters to run like rivers.
medium.q: What miracle provided water for the people?

answers: They had already entered the land
They questioned whether God could furnish a table in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Their question, “Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?” expressed doubt.
medium.q: Why did asking for food test God?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes their sinful rebellion against God.
medium.q: What does “provoking the most High” mean in this context?

answers: God’s many mercies are set beside the people’s continuing sins
There is only a contrast between day and night
There is little water but much water
challenge.explanation: God divided the sea, led them, and gave water, yet they continued to sin.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in this section?

answers: Unbelief and lack of trust in God’s salvation
A desire to keep the commandments
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes that they believed not in God and trusted not in His salvation.
challenge.q: What did the people’s question reveal about their faith?

answers: They had never been in the wilderness
God had already shown that He could provide for them in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Providing water from the rock demonstrated God’s power and care.
challenge.q: Why does the water from the rock strengthen the criticism of their demand for food?

easy.explanation: He rained down manna for them to eat.
easy.q: What did God rain down upon the people?

easy.explanation: The passage says He sent them meat and feathered fowls.
easy.q: What kind of birds did God send?

easy.explanation: They were not estranged from their lust even after being filled.
easy.q: What happened after the people ate and were filled?

medium.explanation: He gave them manna and meat to the full.
medium.q: How did God treat the people’s needs despite their rebellion?

answers: God’s wrath came upon them and many were slain
medium.explanation: God’s wrath came upon them and smote the chosen men of Israel.
medium.q: What resulted from their lust and sin?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the heavenly food God provided.
medium.q: What does “the corn of heaven” refer to?

answers: The problem was lust and unbelief, not merely hunger
They were not in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: They received abundant provision but still sinned and did not believe.
challenge.q: What does the people’s sin after receiving food emphasize?

answers: Entry into the land, battle, and rest
challenge.explanation: God provided food; the people desired more, sinned, and were punished.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the passage?

answers: They finished their days in peace
Their sin brought troubled and shortened lives
challenge.explanation: Their days were consumed in vanity and their years in trouble.
challenge.q: What is meant by their years ending “in trouble”?

answers: They sought and returned to Him
easy.explanation: They sought Him, returned, and enquired early after God.
easy.q: What did the people do when God slew them?

answers: They flattered Him and lied with their tongues
easy.explanation: They flattered Him with their mouths and lied with their tongues.
easy.q: How did they speak to God?

answers: He forgave their iniquity and destroyed them not
easy.explanation: God was full of compassion and did not destroy them.
easy.q: How did God respond despite their weakness?

answers: Their hearts were not right and they were not steadfast in the covenant
medium.explanation: Their words changed, but their hearts were not right with God.
medium.q: Why was the people’s repentance incomplete?

answers: That they were flesh and their life was fleeting
medium.explanation: He remembered that they were flesh, like a passing wind.
medium.q: What did God remember when He showed mercy?

answers: God did not see their sin
God restrained the full measure of His anger
medium.explanation: He repeatedly turned away His anger and did not unleash all His wrath.
medium.q: What does it mean that God “did not stir up all his wrath”?

answers: Their repentance was outward, while God mercifully restrained judgment
The people were faithful while God was only angry
challenge.explanation: Their mouths spoke falsely, yet God showed compassion and withheld total destruction.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the people’s repentance and God’s compassion?

answers: God recognized human weakness and the brevity of life
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes human frailty and mortality.
challenge.q: What does “they were but flesh” reveal about God’s attitude?

answers: Distress, seeking God, incomplete repentance, and mercy
challenge.explanation: The people turned to God in trouble, but their faithfulness remained incomplete; God still showed mercy.
challenge.q: What repeated pattern is described?

paragraphs.title: Forgetting Redemption and the Plagues of Egypt

easy.explanation: They remembered not His hand or the day He delivered them from the enemy.
easy.q: What did the people forget?

easy.explanation: God turned their rivers and floods into blood.
easy.q: What did the rivers become?

easy.explanation: God smote all the firstborn in Egypt.
easy.q: Who was smitten in Egypt?

answers: A renewed account of His signs in Egypt
An account of a new king
A description of settling at Shiloh
medium.explanation: The psalm recounts the signs and wonders God performed in Egypt.
medium.q: What follows the statement that the people forgot God’s deliverance?

medium.explanation: The passage mentions blood, flies, frogs, caterpillars, and locusts among the plagues.
medium.q: Which sequence of plagues appears in the passage?

medium.explanation: The signs are the miraculous works God performed in Egypt.
medium.q: What does “signs” mean in this context?

answers: To bring God’s redeeming power back to their memory
To explain the building of the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The list of plagues reminds the people of God’s power in delivering them.
challenge.q: Why are the plagues recalled after the people forgot God’s deliverance?

answers: Many areas are struck, including water, animals, crops, and the firstborn
It describes only a wilderness journey
challenge.explanation: The plagues affect rivers, creatures, crops, livestock, and the firstborn.
challenge.q: What characterizes the description of the plagues?

answers: Forgetting deliverance creates the need to remember God’s works
challenge.explanation: The people’s forgetfulness is answered by a detailed reminder of God’s saving acts.
challenge.q: What connection is made between memory and faithfulness?

paragraphs.title: The Exodus and Entry into the Land

easy.explanation: He made His people go forth like sheep and guided them like a flock.
easy.q: How did God lead His people through the wilderness?

easy.explanation: The sea overwhelmed their enemies.
easy.q: What overwhelmed the enemies?

answers: He invited them into the wilderness
He left them in the land
easy.explanation: He cast out the heathen before Israel.
easy.q: What did God do to the nations before Israel?

medium.explanation: He divided them an inheritance by line and made the tribes dwell in their tents.
medium.q: What did God give the tribes after casting out the nations?

answers: He led, protected, brought them to the land, and allotted an inheritance
He punished, abandoned, and forgot them
He chose David, left Shiloh, and divided the sea
medium.explanation: The passage describes God’s guidance, protection, bringing Israel to the land, and allotting it.
medium.q: Which sequence describes God’s actions?

answers: The holy land to which God brought His people
The edge of the sea only
medium.explanation: It refers to the land and mountain God brought Israel to possess.
medium.q: What does “the border of his sanctuary” refer to?

answers: God led and protected His people
challenge.explanation: The image presents God as the shepherd and guardian of His people.
challenge.q: What does the image of Israel as sheep emphasize?

answers: Both show God protecting and advancing Israel
challenge.explanation: God protected Israel from enemies and then brought the people toward their inheritance.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the sea overwhelming the enemies and entering the land?

answers: The land was given without order
God’s leadership included an organized settlement for the tribes
The tribes remained in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The inheritance was measured and assigned so the tribes could dwell in their tents.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from dividing the land among the tribes?

paragraphs.title: Rebellion in the Land and the Abandonment of Shiloh

easy.explanation: They tempted and provoked the most high God and kept not His testimonies.
easy.q: What did Israel do in the land?

easy.explanation: They provoked Him with high places and graven images.
easy.q: What provoked God to anger?

easy.explanation: He forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh.
easy.q: What did God forsake?

medium.explanation: They were turned aside like a deceitful bow.
medium.q: What were Israel compared to after their rebellion?

medium.explanation: He delivered His strength into captivity and His glory into the enemy’s hand.
medium.q: What did God deliver into the enemy’s hand?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “Their priests fell by the sword.”
medium.q: What happened to the priests?

answers: Rebellion and false worship led to rejection and the forsaking of the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The people’s rebellion and idolatry are followed by God’s rejection and the forsaking of Shiloh.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between idolatry and the abandonment of Shiloh?

challenge.explanation: A deceitful bow fails to perform as expected, picturing Israel’s unfaithfulness.
challenge.q: What does the image of a “deceitful bow” mean?

answers: Rebellion, God’s rejection, abandonment of Shiloh, and defeat
Water, manna, and entry into the land
challenge.explanation: Israel rebelled, God rejected them and forsook Shiloh, and the people and their leaders suffered defeat.
challenge.q: Which sequence of consequences appears in the passage?

easy.explanation: God chose the tribe of Judah.
easy.q: Which tribe did God choose?

easy.explanation: He chose Mount Zion, which He loved.
easy.q: Which place did God choose?

easy.explanation: God took David from the sheepfolds.
easy.q: From where did God take David?

medium.explanation: David was chosen to feed Jacob and Israel, God’s inheritance.
medium.q: Why was David chosen?

answers: Integrity of heart and skilfulness of hands
medium.explanation: He fed them according to the integrity of his heart and guided them by skilful hands.
medium.q: With what qualities did David lead the people?

answers: To shepherd, lead, and care for the people
medium.explanation: “To feed” is shepherd language for leading and caring for God’s people.
medium.q: What does “to feed” mean in this context?

answers: God refused Joseph and Ephraim but chose Judah, Zion, and David
God chose all the tribes equally in this passage
God rejected Judah and chose Ephraim
challenge.explanation: The passage says God refused the tabernacle of Joseph and chose not Ephraim, but chose Judah and Zion.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between Joseph and Ephraim and Judah?

answers: Leadership has nothing to do with caring for others
A shepherd became a leader who cared for God’s people
challenge.explanation: David’s shepherding work becomes an image of his care and leadership of Israel.
challenge.q: What does David’s movement from the sheepfolds to leadership emphasize?

answers: The heart matters only in battle
Good leadership joins inward integrity with practical wisdom
challenge.explanation: David led with integrity of heart and skillful hands, joining character with ability.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the integrity of David’s heart and the skill of his hands?
